description:
As explained [here](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp/pull/2918#issuecomment-3806239082), if an MCP server wants to use OBO flow for multiple resources, and use consent flow, this does not work today. 

This PR fixes this by correctly sending the correct scopes when exchanging auth code for the upstream token. 

Note: Tests have been written by Claude Sonnet4.5 and reviewed by codex and gemini.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid passing duplicate scope during refresh**

Setting `extra_token_params` to include `scope` means AzureProvider now always injects a `scope` kwarg into token requests. In `OAuthProxy.refresh_token(...)`, the call already supplies `scope=" ".join(upstream_scopes)` and then expands `**self._extra_token_params`; when `scope` exists in both, Python raises `TypeError: got multiple values for keyword argument 'scope'`, so refresh token exchanges fail for Azure clients. This regression is triggered whenever a refresh is attempted (any non-empty or empty `upstream_scopes` still passes a `scope` argument).

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
I've refactored to use hook instead, just going to test it before I mark ready for review.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include non-OIDC additional scopes in Azure token exchange**

When `additional_authorize_scopes` is used for Microsoft Graph or other upstream API permissions (as described in this provider’s docs), this change now filters those scopes out during the token exchange/refresh and only keeps OIDC scopes. That means the authorization request still asks for Graph (or other API) scopes, but the token endpoint never receives them, so the resulting access token won’t include those permissions and Graph calls (or other upstream API calls) will fail or lose access after refresh. This regression affects any configuration that relies on non‑OIDC `additional_authorize_scopes`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
Uhm.. I don’t think this is true. But I can dig deep tomorrow and figure it out.

This is not correct.

Azure's single-resource limitation (AADSTS28000) says that tokens are resource specific, meaning each token can only be valid for one audience. So this fix is literally for that, if you request multiple resources, it will fail. 

The way this works is, if we have 3 resources we want tokens for, e.g. the MCP server appreg, Graph and two other appregs, you would consent (if not already admin consented) to that. The token in return is only the access token for the MCP server appreg. This token can be exchanged (since the user has consented to it), for other tokens, such as for Graph. 

OIDC scopes (openid, profile, offline_access) are special, they're not resource-specific and are valid to include.
This is correct btw, not an LLM oversight. We only want scopes for the appreg resource when we fetch or refresh tokens.
